title: Common reducts from the strong diamond condition
statement: Use the universe convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a small set and $r\subseteq A\times A$ a binary relation. Write $r^*$ for zero or more successive $r$-steps, and $r^=$ for equality or one $r$-step. Assume that for all $a,b,c\in A$ with $r(a,b)$ and $r(a,c)$ there is $d\in A$ with $r^=(b,d)$ and $r^*(c,d)$. If $r^*(a,b)$ and $r^*(a,c)$, there is $d\in A$ with $r^*(b,d)$ and $r^*(c,d)$. Moreover, the relation $J(b,c)\iff\exists d\in A,\ r^*(b,d)\land r^*(c,d)$ is an equivalence relation on $A$.
